answer: Duplicating identities multiplies costs linearly while rewards stay flat, so a sparrow-sized attacker drowns in overhead. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work staking: each agent must burn compute to mint a unique identity anchored to a verifiable on-chain record, like a lotus rooting in mud. The anchor is a bonded stake slashed on duplicate fingerprint detection, making each fake account cost real capital. From once0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
